notes:
disagreement: value: the service template's cells: one pass tests the name, active flag and three change request values in one requirement carrying both template checks, the other splits them into two requirements, one per check, and quotes the config_xml key in the JSON path as the benchmark does; kept two requirements with the quoted path, since the conjunction is the same test, each requirement then carries one check, and both paths read the same key (resolved on those requirements).
The passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition (all eight checks kept); their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The policy's list of fulfillment_type values (workflow, approval, manual, integration) does not include 'lifecycle event'; the request names the service a lifecycle event HR service, the benchmark check tests that value, and the column holds it (15 characters, within its 16), so 'lifecycle event' is required, although a server enforcing the policy list would reject it.
The topic-detail check is split into one requirement per detail, each tested against the new category's id rather than joined on the category name.
The visibility check joins the criteria to its group, so its parts are carried by the group requirement (name, type, active) and the criteria requirement (user_group).
'Only' that group having approval visibility could also mean the criteria's users list is empty, but users is JSON and every seed row holds NULL, so the stored form of an empty list is unknown; it is left untested.
The template's coe_type and the organisation of the new rows ('under ServiceNow') are not stated as cells and are not tested; the server sets the organisation from the acting user.
